prompt.context: It is summer 2012 and your client is a healthcare delivery system in North Carolina that is currently in a strong financial situation but anticipates a 30% decline in revenue over the next few years.
prompt.question: How can you help them protect their margins in the future?

clarifying_info.q: What does Piedmont Health do and what is their network structure?
clarifying_info.a: Piedmont Health is a network of affiliate hospitals, specialty care centers, medical foundations (groups of physicians), university and research centers in NC only. It is not-for-profit and primarily serves low-income communities. No one is ever turned away from services. It has grown significantly over the past 20 years by acquiring affiliates.

clarifying_info.q: Do they have significant write-offs or uncollected revenue?
clarifying_info.a: Currently, Piedmont Health writes off $5 billion in uncollected payments for provided care.

clarifying_info.q: What is driving the expected revenue decline?
clarifying_info.a: With the recent passing of the Affordable Care Act and other anticipated federal and state legislation, not-for-profit hospitals can expect to see an increase in uncompensated care and a decrease in reimbursement amounts by Medicare.

clarifying_info.q: Are they interested in growing top-line revenue or exploring new revenue streams?
clarifying_info.a: They are not interested in top-line growth, product mix, or different revenue streams. The focus is on capturing typically lost revenue and improving their cost structure.

framework: Prevent revenue losses: address billing inefficiencies and collections to reduce write-offs
Cut costs: energy efficiency, biomedical asset management, supply chain consolidation, workforce redundancy elimination
Root cause: the network of affiliates acquired over 20 years each operates independently, creating redundant and overlapping business processes that drive higher costs and lower revenue capture

questions.prompt: What areas should the candidate explore to protect margins?
questions.guidance: The candidate should identify two main levers: (1) capturing revenue currently being lost (billing/collections) and (2) reducing costs across the consolidated network. Strong candidates will note the overarching theme of lack of standardization across acquired affiliates as the key driver of both revenue leakage and excess cost.

questions.prompt: How significant is the revenue write-off problem, and what does that suggest as a priority?
questions.guidance: $5B written off out of $20B revenue = 25% of revenue is uncollected. This is a massive opportunity. Candidates should recognize that even partial improvement in collections has outsized margin impact relative to cost cuts.

math.answer: 25% of revenue is currently written off — a significant opportunity to capture lost revenue.

brainstorming.prompt: What specific recommendations would you make to prevent revenue losses and cut costs?

categories.name: Prevent Revenue Losses — Billing
ideas: Standardize and clarify billing processes across all affiliates to prevent denials from Medicare and other payers
Reduce time from date of care to date a bill is sent to accelerate cash collection
Implement system-wide billing software or shared services center to replace fragmented affiliate billing

categories.name: Prevent Revenue Losses — Collections & Financial Counseling
ideas: Expand collections office to include more financial counselors
Provide financial advice, guidance, and help setting up payment plans for low-income patients
Proactive outreach to patients before bills become overdue

categories.name: Cut Costs — Energy Efficiency
ideas: Put computer and medical equipment in sleep mode or turn off when not in use
Remove one fluorescent bulb per multi-bulb fixture where lighting remains adequate to reduce electricity and bulb costs
Investigate utility purchasing plans (fixed vs. variable rates) if utilities in the state are deregulated

categories.name: Cut Costs — Biomedical Asset Management
ideas: Invest in small GPS trackers to locate equipment (e.g., wheelchairs) throughout facilities and alert if leaving premises
Use tracking data for utilization analysis to inform future purchasing decisions rather than defaulting to bed-count-based purchasing
Loss prevention: prevent theft and accidental disposal of costly equipment like wheelchairs

categories.name: Cut Costs — Supply Chain Consolidation
ideas: Consolidate strategic sourcing and purchasing into a centralized department for the entire health care delivery system
Leverage system-wide buying power to negotiate favorable rates and volume discounts with suppliers

categories.name: Cut Costs — Workforce Analysis
ideas: Consolidate support functions such as Finance and HR across the system
Eliminate redundant headcount across affiliates that currently operate as separate business units
Assess whether shared service centers can replace duplicated back-office roles without business impact

recommendation: Piedmont Health should pursue a two-track strategy: (1) recover lost revenue by standardizing billing and expanding collections/financial counseling, targeting a meaningful reduction of the $5B annual write-off; (2) reduce costs by consolidating the fragmented back-office and supply chain operations of its acquired affiliates into a unified system

The overarching root cause is the lack of standardization across 20+ years of affiliate acquisitions — addressing this systematically will compound savings across billing, procurement, energy, and workforce
risks: Change management resistance from individual affiliates accustomed to operating independently
Implementation costs and time for new billing/ERP systems across a large network
Risk of service disruption during consolidation of support functions
Regulatory complexity of billing standardization under Medicare/ACA rules
next_steps: Conduct a detailed diagnostic of billing denial rates and write-off root causes by affiliate to prioritize billing fixes
Map supply chain spend across all affiliates to identify quick-win consolidation and negotiate new vendor contracts
Pilot a financial counseling expansion at one or two affiliates and measure impact on collections before system-wide rollout
Commission a workforce analysis to identify consolidation opportunities in Finance, HR, and other support functions without patient-care impact
